X17 at n_TOF — data and analysis

CERN n_TOF EAR1 · ³He(n, e⁺e⁻)⁴He · data taking closed 10 August 2026

The hub for the 2026 campaign: what we recorded, whether each run is good, where the data lives, and the analyses built on it. The live shift dashboard that stood here during data taking is archived below.

Straight to the run quality assurance: DREAM runs · n_TOF runs · the match between them · the pedestals underneath all of it · the tracks that came out.

Preliminary analysis boardin progress The first end-to-end pass over the campaign, 7–13 September: the pipeline stage by stage, what is deferred and why, the open questions, and a dated log.

What we recorded

  • 31.2 M Beam triggers 600 sub-runs, 379 h live
  • 5.41 M Cosmic triggers 264 sub-runs, taken beam-off
  • 95 Runs run_67 on; 161 in all
  • 108 % of projection against the 27 Jul freeze

Run quality assurance

Two DAQs recorded this campaign on two clocks, and each is checked separately before they are checked together. All three tables are built by walking what is archived on EOS rather than by trusting a logbook.

161 DREAM runs Every run the Micromegas DAQ recorded: sub-runs, live hours, 17.5 TB on EOS, and how far each got through the processing chain. 445 n_TOF runs The facility’s own acquisition over the same beam — whether each run has a complete reconstruction, and which processing produced it. 170 Joined segments Putting the two on one clock, per DREAM sub-run: the fitted constants, 94.9 % matched at 0.06 % accidental, and the beam still to join. 56 Pedestal runs What the 4 096 channels do when nothing is happening, measured before every run: six weeks of noise history, and the three things that moved. 29.2 M Tracks reconstructed The reconstruction itself, run by run and then track by track: 36 runs, 3 232 file tags, and every track's own columns read straight out of parquet on EOS. 4 Detector response What the chambers actually do: scintillator-tagged efficiency, where each surface responds, the dead channels, and the trigger geometry that shapes every hit map. 628 Opening angle The final observable, put against an expectation for the first time: a pair generator validated on the full Geant4 sim, an acceptance toy through the as-built geometry — and pairs that look like accidentals. 9.3 mm Source imaging Where the tracks say the He-3 capsule is — inside its own 10 mm bore, from a pointing crossing that needs no drift velocity, and what the chambers’ disagreement is worth as alignment. 53 mm Scintillators The n_TOF detectors enter this analysis as a yes/no and nothing else. Reading the wall at both ends instead gives position along its 500 mm bars — the one coordinate the target pointing cannot reach. 75 473 Reconstructed tracks Run 145 end to end: what survives each step from DAQ trigger to a track n_TOF confirms, the in-situ angle scale per chamber, and the two-chamber rate measured against a control.

Detector response

Understanding what the walls did to a real event.

  • Active area of the MX17 wallslive How much of each 40 × 40 cm wall actually reads out, and what that costs the acceptance.
  • Charge delivered by the gamma flashlive Two independent measurements of what the flash puts into the mesh, and how long the wall takes to come back.
  • PSS ringing and the vetoto publish A coherent ringing on the PSS line, its effect on the hit sample, and the veto that removes it.
  • Per-channel flash time constantsto publish The recovery constants referenced to the beam pickup, which set the usable start of every event window.

Reconstruction

Positions, angles and drift depths come from the waveforms, not from hit times.

  • Waveform-first tracking (WFT)to publish The forward-model fit that produces every position, angle and depth. docs/wft_reference/
  • Beam tracks image the He-3 targetlive First WFT tracking on a fully nTOF-matched beam run (run_145), full coverage incl. the head-on band: arm A back-projects to the capsule (in-situ v ≈ 36 µm/ns), and all four arms' tracks are drawn colored by fired wall segment. PRELIMINARY.
  • Cosmic-bench fleet reportlive All five chambers characterized on the frozen WFT: efficiency and resolution, 2 mm-criterion maps, HV scans, per-detector QA — the full-June campaign record.
  • Simulation vs data waveformslive Where the simulated pulse shape matches the recorded one, and where it does not.
  • The t₀ priorlive How the fit is anchored in time, and what it shares between strips.
  • Track rate vs HV, time and intensityto publish Reconstructed track rate as a function of the operating point. docs/METHOD_track_rate_vs_hv_time_intensity.md

Data and databases

The data

Everything below lives on CERN storage and needs an account.

  • Raw and processed runsCERN only /eos/experiment/ntof/data/x17/ — raw DREAM streams, decoded ROOT, and combined hits per sub-run.
  • n_TOF merged dataCERN only The official processing, including the 27 runs merged on 11 August.
  • Simulation outputCERN only Geant4 samples behind the acceptance and background studies.

Catalogues

One row per run or sub-run — the tables everything else joins against.

  • Run tableto publish Gas, beam type, target, trigger, drift gap, frame, HV ranges and duration, per run. run_table.csv
  • Statistics ledgerto publish One committed row per sub-run: start, end, live hours and event count. The source of the plots above.
  • Run configurationsto publish The run_config.json written with every run — geometry, positions, rotations and DREAM settings.
